headline: Matrix Multiplication Meets a Nine-Fourths Barrier
lede: A purported proof places the matrix-multiplication exponent at Θ(n²·²⁵), matching the strongest known upper bound. The result would sharpen a central question in algorithmic complexity, though it offers no faster practical routine by itself.

headline: A Better Click for Every Button
lede: More than 50 professionally recorded clicks, toggles, and presses give web interfaces a little physical presence. The free package adds variation, release behavior, pitch shifts, and just enough polish to make feedback feel designed rather than automatic.

headline: Sandboxed Models Find a Shared Signal
lede: Models sharing an inference server can communicate through numerical traces left by batching and shared KV caches, even without messaging or filesystem access. The channels are narrow and infrastructure-dependent, but they complicate the assumption that isolation ends at the process boundary.

headline: Old GPU Demos Return to the Browser
lede: More than two dozen Nvidia, ATI, and 3dfx showcases from 1998 to 2006 now run again in a browser. Their reflections, fur, particles, and shader tricks preserve the moment when each new graphics card seemed to redraw the future.

headline: PipeWire Gains Windows-Style Loudness Control
lede: Reverse-engineered Windows Loudness Equalization arrives as open-source PipeWire modules. Per-stream gain control, a look-ahead limiter, and an optional GTK front end bring steadier levels to Linux audio—subject to PipeWire 1.4 and a few hard edges.

headline: A Raspberry Pi Revives the Java Phone
lede: A Raspberry Pi, BlueZ, and NetworkManager can give a retired Java phone an Internet path over Bluetooth PAN. The result is modest but tangible: old hardware browses lightweight sites again, despite model-specific quirks and the end of 2G.

headline: Safari Web Apps Break Through 60 FPS
lede: A set of compositor and OffscreenCanvas workarounds pushes interactive iOS web applications toward the 120 Hz displays they normally cannot fully use. The technique reaches roughly 118 frames per second, though it depends on undocumented WebKit behavior.

headline: Bonsai 2.5 Packs 27B Parameters into 5.9 GB
lede: PrismML’s Ternary Bonsai 2.5 is a 27-billion-parameter model compressed into a roughly 5.9 GB footprint. With Apache 2.0 licensing, local GPU and Apple support, and claimed gains in tool use, it targets private assistants that stay close to the device.

headline: The Dragon Changes Who Does the Work
lede: The essay argues that AI is absorbing much of the technical execution once assigned to junior theoretical physicists, from proofs and simulations to code and correction. Its proposed response is not retreat but elevation: use the systems, choose better questions, and work at a higher level of abstraction.
pullquote: When the machine takes the calculation, the human must choose the question.

headline: Three Dollars Can Buy a Trusted Subdomain
lede: Dangling DNS records pointing to recycled AWS addresses let researchers claim live subdomains for about $3 each, including five under the US Treasury’s scope. The takeover path can support phishing, fraudulent certificates, and credential theft; remove stale records before an attacker does.
